transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. —. What brings you in today?
Hello, Doctor. For the past few years I feel worn out all the time, like I’m running on empty even when I’m not doing that much. It just feels like a constant struggle to get through the day.

Have these low-energy and worn-out feelings been present most days for at least two weeks at a time, or have they come and gone over the years? Also, have you had similar episodes before that fully went away and then returned?

These worn-out and low feelings have been with me pretty steadily, almost every day, for a little over three years now since my company restructured. They don't really come and go; it has just been a constant, heavy cloud. I've never had an episode like this before in my life.
During these three years, have you also had periods of at least two months when your mood and energy felt back to normal, or has the low mood been present most days the whole time?

No, I haven't had any breaks where I felt back to normal at all. Even when we took vacations, this heavy, gray feeling stayed with me, and there certainly haven't been any periods as long as two months where I felt like my old self.
During this time, have you also had other symptoms like poor sleep, changes in appetite, low self-esteem, poor concentration, or feeling hopeless?

I definitely feel hopeless, like this flat, tired state is just how my life is going to be now and nothing will change it, and my concentration is so poor that I'm making small errors in reports that used to take me just an afternoon. My sleep is generally okay, though it never refreshes me, and I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where your symptoms became much more severe, with clear loss of interest or pleasure, and significant changes in sleep, appetite, or functioning beyond your usual low mood?

No, I haven't really experienced a specific two-week block where things suddenly became much more severe or different. It has just been a constant, steady, and flat low mood and fatigue that has persisted pretty evenly over the last three years.
Have there ever been any periods of at least 2 months during these 3 years when your mood and energy were back to normal, or has the low mood been present most days without any real break?

No, there have been no breaks at all where I felt back to normal for two months or more. This low, gray feeling has been completely steady and constant over the last three years. Even when we went on vacation, the heavy cloud and fatigue never really lifted.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 years when you felt mostly normal, or has this low mood and fatigue been present for most of the time over many years without a long break?

No, I haven't had any breaks or felt normal at all since this started a little over three years ago. Before my company's restructuring, I felt like my usual self, but since then, this low mood and fatigue have been constant without any relief.
Before this started three years ago, did you ever have at least two full years when you felt mostly well and not depressed or worn out? Or has this low mood been present for most of your adult life?

Yes, before the restructuring three years ago, I felt well, active, and engaged for many years, enjoying my hikes, painting, and planning trips. This low, worn-out feeling is definitely a change that started about three years ago, rather than something I've struggled with my entire adult life.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during these three years when your mood and energy were back to normal, or has the low mood been present most days the whole time?

No, I really haven't had any periods of normal mood or energy lasting anywhere near two months over these three years. This low, gray feeling has been present pretty steadily almost every single day. Even when we took trips abroad, it failed to restore my energy or bring back my normal self.
During these three years, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hiking, painting, or planning trips?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in those activities. I stopped my weekend hikes and painting sessions because I feel too drained, and even planning trips or taking photos of the hills has lost its joy and just feels gray and flat.

Have you had any periods of at least two weeks during these three years when your mood was clearly worse than usual, with several symptoms like very low energy, sleep or appetite changes, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or thoughts of death?

No, I haven't had any severe two-week spikes or deeper plunges where things got even worse. My low, gray mood and lack of energy have just been very steady and constant over these last three years. I haven't experienced any major changes in appetite or any thoughts of death.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least 2 months during the past 3 years when you felt back to your normal self, with little or no depression or fatigue? Or has the low mood been present most of the time without any long break?

No, I haven't had any break like that at all; it has been completely steady and constant for the past three years. Even on vacations or trips abroad, I never truly felt back to my normal self. The low, gray feeling and fatigue just never lifted.
Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days where you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or became more impulsive than normal?

No, I have never felt unusually energized or euphoric like that. My experience has been the complete opposite, where I just feel constantly low and drained. I've definitely never had any periods where I felt hyperactive or needed less sleep.
Do you find that you have become more self-critical or feel inadequate compared with others, even when you know the situation is not your fault?
I haven't really thought about it that way, and I don't tend to compare myself to others. I mostly just worry about my own work performance slipping and how tired I feel all the time.
Over the past two weeks, has your mood been so low that you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, with marked loss of interest or pleasure in almost everything?

Yes, I have felt that way nearly every day, but it has actually been going on much longer than just the past two weeks—it's been a steady, heavy cloud for over three years. Everything just feels gray and joyless, and I've lost all interest in things I used to love, like planning trips or taking photos of the hills.
Before this started three years ago, did you ever have a period of at least two years when you felt depressed or low most days, or was this the first and only episode?

Yes, this is the first and only time I have ever felt this way. Before the company restructuring a little over three years ago, I had never experienced a period of feeling depressed or low for years. This current episode is the very first time I've ever gone through something like this.
Have these symptoms caused problems in your work, relationships, or daily activities, or have you been able to keep functioning mostly as usual despite feeling low?

Yes, they have definitely caused problems. At work, my reviews have slipped from "exceeds" to "meets" expectations because I keep making small mistakes and having to stay late to fix them. In my personal life, I've backed out of hobbies and social plans, which has caused tension with my husband and left me feeling like I'm just existing instead of really living.
Have there been any periods during the past three years when your symptoms were much worse for at least two weeks, or has it been a steady low mood without any clear major worsening?

No, there haven't been any sharp waves or two-week periods where things got significantly worse. It has just been a constant, flat, gray baseline that has persisted steadily for the last three years since my company's restructuring.

Have you had any significant changes in sleep, appetite, weight, or energy that are especially severe, such as sleeping much more or less than usual, eating much more or less, or losing/gaining weight without trying?

My energy levels are extremely low and I feel completely drained, like my body is filled with sand, even though a full night of sleep never seems to restore me. I haven't noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight, though.
Over the past few weeks, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, thoughts of harming yourself, or any wish to be dead?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or wishing to be dead. Even though I feel very hopeless and flat about the future, those kinds of thoughts haven't crossed my mind. I just feel completely exhausted and stuck.

Because your symptoms have lasted more than two years, I want to clarify: have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during this time when you felt back to your normal self, with little or no depressed mood or fatigue?

No, I haven't had any period of relief at all, let alone two months. This low, gray, and exhausted feeling has been completely constant and steady over the last three-plus years. Even when I took vacations or time off, I never felt back to my normal self.

During this three-year period, have you had at least two weeks where you felt much worse than your usual low mood, with several symptoms like marked loss of interest, sleep or appetite changes, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or thoughts of death?

No, I haven't experienced any distinct two-week periods where things got significantly worse than my usual state. It has just been a constant, flat, gray feeling over the last three years without any sudden drops or changes.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything you used to enjoy, or do you still get some enjoyment from activities even though you feel low?

Yes, I've lost almost all interest and pleasure in the things I used to love, and everything just feels completely gray and joyless now. I no longer enjoy hiking, painting, or taking photos of the Temecula hills, and even our vacations have failed to bring back any sense of enjoyment.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during these three years when you felt back to your normal self, with little or no depressed mood or fatigue?

No, I haven't had any period like that at all where I felt normal. This heavy, exhausted feeling has been completely constant and steady over the last three years, without any breaks. Even during vacations or time off, I never truly felt like my old self or regained my energy.
Have you been sleeping more than usual, or do you wake up feeling unrefreshed even after a full night of sleep?

I wake up feeling completely unrefreshed, even after a full night of sleep. I go through the day feeling completely drained, as if my body is filled with heavy sand. By the time I log off from work, I have absolutely no energy left to do anything.
Have you had any significant changes in appetite or weight, or problems with sleep such as sleeping much more or much less than usual?

I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight. As for my sleep, I generally sleep a full night but just wake up feeling completely unrefreshed and drained anyway, rather than sleeping much more or less than usual.
During these past three years, have you also felt very low in self-esteem or felt like a failure, or has it mostly been hopelessness and fatigue without those feelings?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought about it in terms of self-esteem or feeling like a failure. For me, it has mostly just been this constant, heavy fatigue and a deep sense of hopelessness that my life is always going to feel this flat and drained.
During this time, have you often felt worthless, like a failure, or very hard on yourself, even when things were not your fault?
No, I haven't really felt worthless or like a failure. I do, however, worry a lot about my work performance slipping and making mistakes lately.
